title: Pathfinding may use more than 4 threads
evidence: Additional threads increase memory consumption and synchronization time
suggestion: Lower navigation/pathfinding/max_threads toward 4 unless queries are actually waiting. The description says extra threads copy data.
tradeoff: Fewer path queries run at once.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: Pathfinding threads are unlimited
suggestion: Set navigation/pathfinding/max_threads to a finite count. The description says -1 means unlimited and extra threads cost memory.
tradeoff: Path queries queue instead of spawning without a cap.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: Navigation map sync runs on the main thread
evidence: avoids stalling the main thread but adds an additional delay
suggestion: Turn navigation/world/map_use_async_iterations on so map sync leaves the main thread. The description says the async path avoids that stall.
tradeoff: Map changes show up one step later.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: Avoidance is not using multiple threads
evidence: If enabled the avoidance calculations use multiple threads
suggestion: Turn navigation/avoidance/thread_model/avoidance_use_multiple_threads on when many agents avoid each other.
tradeoff: Avoidance shares the threads it is given.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: A NavigationAgent2D/3D has avoidance enabled
evidence: Avoidance processing with many registered agents has a significant performance cost
suggestion: Turn avoidance_enabled off on 2D or 3D agents that do not currently need avoidance. Cost depends on active agents and nearby neighbours.
tradeoff: Those agents no longer receive safe_velocity.
expected_effect: scan_scene should show a lower count after the edit. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

tradeoff: Depends on which objects or allocations you remove.

title: Navigation regions synchronize on the main thread
evidence: navigation/world/region_use_async_iterations is false. Godot docs: "By default, the regions in a NavigationServer map now update asynchronously using threads to improve performance."
suggestion: Turn navigation/world/region_use_async_iterations back on so region changes synchronize on a background thread.
tradeoff: Region changes take effect after an extra delay.
expected_effect: Re-measure with collect_metrics after changing this setting. No frame-time percentage is predicted.

title: A navigation obstacle is both static and dynamic
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: A NavigationObstacle2D/3D with avoidance enabled has both a radius (dynamic) and an outline of three or more vertices (static). Godot docs: "While both static and dynamic properties can be active at the same time on the same obstacle this is not recommended for performance."
suggestion: Use the radius while the obstacle moves and the vertices once it rests, as the page describes, instead of both at once.
tradeoff: Switching between the two needs a script.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A TileMapLayer creates many per-cell navigation regions
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled TileMapLayer with navigation_enabled has more than 256 inspected cell/layer navigation polygons containing baked polygons or outlines and nonzero navigation layers. Both native versions create a region per qualifying cell and navigation layer. This is an object-count review cutoff, not a measured pathfinding or map-synchronization cost. Runtime tile-data overrides and scene-collection sources are skipped; resource/cell inspection limits are reported.
suggestion: For a mostly static level, compare a consolidated NavigationRegion2D bake and disable per-cell navigation only after the replacement preserves valid paths.
tradeoff: Baking changes update granularity, connectivity and layer handling. Preserve doors, streaming and dynamic edits, and avoid overlapping old and replacement regions.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A GridMap creates many per-cell navigation regions
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: A GridMap with bake_navigation enabled has more than 256 inspected cells referencing nonempty item navigation meshes with nonzero navigation layers. Native octant updates create a NavigationServer3D region per qualifying cell. The cutoff is a review heuristic; map synchronization and path cost are not measured. At most 4096 cells across qualifying GridMaps are inspected and omitted cells are reported.
suggestion: For static levels, compare baking a consolidated NavigationRegion3D from the level geometry, then disable per-cell GridMap navigation only after the replacement works.
tradeoff: Consolidation changes bake/update granularity, navigation layers and region boundaries. Preserve dynamic doors, streaming and path connectivity, and avoid overlapping old and replacement navigation.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A navigation region contains a large polygon graph
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An enabled NavigationRegion3D with nonzero navigation layers has more than 8192 baked navigation polygons. Native path queries search polygon connections; polygon count bounds graph size but is not the number visited by each query. This reads stored polygon count without rebaking the mesh. The cutoff is heuristic.
suggestion: Profile long and unreachable path requests, then simplify unnecessary navigation geometry on flat areas while preserving routes and agent clearance.
tradeoff: Coarser navigation geometry can remove narrow routes or change paths. Splitting into regions without reducing polygons does not automatically reduce query work.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: Avoidance agents allow more neighbours than the default
heuristic_rationale: A configured feature is a measurement candidate, not proof that it is currently visible, costly or unnecessary. Numeric review thresholds are Render Lens heuristics, not Godot limits.
evidence: An avoidance-enabled NavigationAgent2D/3D searches a positive distance and allows more than ten neighbours. Godot's RVO code retains up to max_neighbors candidates and builds a constraint for each retained neighbour. Ten is the default-based review cutoff; actual nearby agents determine work.
suggestion: Compare a smaller neighbour limit in representative dense crowds and profile CPU avoidance time.
tradeoff: Too few neighbours can cause collisions, unstable crowd movement or poor avoidance.
expected_effect: Potentially reduce work for this feature; no frame-time saving is predicted from configuration alone.
verify_step: Capture a visual reference; change one feature and repeat frame timing plus relevant CPU or GPU profiling in the same scene on target hardware.

title: A navigation mesh cell is smaller than its map's
evidence: Godot prints "A navigation mesh that uses a `cell_size` of 0.1 was assigned to a navigation map set to a larger `cell_size` of 0.25." when a NavigationRegion's mesh uses a cell_size or cell_height below the map's (the navigation/2d or 3d default_cell_size and default_cell_height settings for default maps). The message says the mismatch can cause rasterization errors with navigation mesh edges on the map.
suggestion: Bake the navigation mesh with the map's cell size and height, or change the map defaults to match.
tradeoff: Matching a coarser map cell size lowers navigation mesh precision.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output

title: Static obstacle vertices have Y values that avoidance ignores
evidence: Godot prints "Y coordinates of static obstacle vertices are ignored. Please use obstacle position Y to change elevation of obstacle." in editor builds when a NavigationObstacle3D's vertices have a nonzero Y; avoidance ignores the Y in every build.
suggestion: Keep obstacle vertices at Y 0 and move the obstacle node to set its elevation.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output

title: Navigation is baked at runtime from visual meshes
evidence: Godot prints "Source geometry parsing for navigation mesh baking had to parse RenderingServer meshes at runtime." in a running game when a NavigationMesh parses mesh instances (parsed geometry type Mesh Instances, the default, or Both) and a script bakes or parses source geometry (bake_navigation_mesh or parse_source_geometry_data). Godot's message continues that visual meshes store their geometry on the GPU, so reading it back is slow.
suggestion: Parse static colliders instead (parsed geometry type Static Colliders), or bake in the editor and load the result.
tradeoff: Collision shapes are coarser than visual meshes.
expected_effect: Godot uses the configuration as written instead of overriding or ignoring it; no performance saving is asserted.
verify_step: audit_project_rendering or scan_scene, then run the game and confirm the warning is gone from the output
